status: production implementation with bounded reservation/retile policy
method: Each comparison alternates ordinary completed searches against repeated 64-query calls on one shared generated corpus. Three warmups, fifteen samples, changing queries, cached graphs. CPU checks, three instrumented replays and detailed compilation run after timing. External GPU activity changed throughout. Profile sums are contention-affected diagnostics, not components of ordinary host latency.

policy.notes: Smaller corpora use fewer rows. Reserved query width and k are retained. Tile size follows the largest reserved width when k grows or the corpus changes. Standalone TopK reads caller-owned score storage and retains its separate 262144-column selection tiles.

qualification.execution_note: 59-test full suite plus the subsequently added device-limit test; the expanded 256-query multi-tile standalone TopK test was rerun separately after extension.
coverage: host widths 65/127/128/129/255/256 and invalid tail query
workspace growth, k growth after width reduction, retained score cap
updates, append, shrink/regrow corpus, empty corpus
cached graph replay, masks, sharding, profile and device submissions
standalone TopK 256 queries, ties/nonfinite/missing scores, multi-tile global IDs
prepared-search wide batches, invalid final query, slot reuse
64-query chunk parity for every timed neighbor plus independent CPU scores

comparisons.timing: Alternating completed searches on one corpus with changing queries and cached graphs. Baseline reuses one 64-query worker. CPU checks, detailed compilation and three instrumented stage replays occur after ordinary timings. External GPU activity is uncontrolled.
comparisons.reproduce: HRX_OFFLINE=1 ROWS=1000000 DIM=384 BATCH=128 K=5 SAMPLES=15 OUTPUT=1m-384-b128.json cargo test --locked --release --lib compare_batch_chunks -- --ignored --nocapture
